symptom: Item 4 of saingge's comment on mendixlabs/mxcli#1517 (ako/mxcli#1399): `check -p` printed 'Check passed!' with a 'flow change(s) not predicted — an earlier statement of the script creates or changes it' note, and exec then refused that statement and rolled the whole script back ('Nothing was written: statement 1 was rolled back'). exec's own preflight has the same blind spot, so the refusal came only at write time
cause: checkFlowVerdicts predicted every flow statement against the flow as stored; once an earlier statement touched the same flow it could not know what exec would see there, so it marked the flow 'touched' and gave up on every later statement about it
file: modelsdk/mpr/writer_simulated.go (SimulateWrites, ErrSimulatedWrite), modelsdk/mpr/studiopro_lock.go (guardWrite), modelsdk/mpr/writer_deferred.go (FlushDeferredWrites), mdl/backend/modelsdk/backend.go (SimulateWrites), mdl/executor/validate_flow_verdicts.go (checkFlowVerdicts, flowModifyViolations, alterFlowViolations)
fix: A simulated write mode on the writer: a deferred run (updates held in memory and served back by the reader's overlay) that is never flushed, whose discard clears the overlays, and in which guardWrite refuses every other write before it touches storage. checkFlowVerdicts opens one for the pass; each create-or-modify or alter predicted as spliced has its plan saved into it, and its flow is not marked touched, so the next statement on that flow is predicted against the simulated result. Folder moves and creates still mark the flow touched
test: modelsdk/mpr/writer_simulated_test.go (held update read back, delete and flush refused, disk and transaction id untouched, discard restores, writes land afterwards); mdl/executor/validate_flow_verdicts_chained_pedapp_test.go (refusal of statement 2 predicted, alter addressing what statement 1 wrote predicted to apply, every project file byte-identical across check, stored flow unchanged after check, exec refuses what check predicted). Before the change both chained subtests reported the flow unpredicted
insight: The machinery already existed: the deferred-write run built for access-rule runs (#872) holds updates and serves them back to every read, which is exactly a simulation minus the flush — the only additions are 'never flush' and 'refuse what cannot be held at guardWrite', the choke point every write already passes before touching storage. Two traps when testing: ExecuteProgram has no rollback (that is cmd exec's journal), so an exec-agreement subtest writes statement 1 and must run last; and the simulation's defer has to run before CacheUnitReads' release — it does, being inside checkFlowVerdicts
